clue.text: Batting edge? Shut up

parts.note: in cricket the side batting is said to be in
a side is an edge or border

explanation.surface: A cricketer nicks one off the edge of the bat and is told to keep quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the team batting is 'in'. The question mark flags that 'Batting edge' is not a cricket shot here.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone shut up is locked away, as in prison, which is informally being inside.

clue.text: International agreement accepting mass repercussions?

definitions.note: plural in the clue; the answer is a mass noun for the effects of something

indicators.note: the agreement takes in the letter for mass

parts.note: a pact is a formal agreement

explanation.surface: A global treaty takes in a large number of consequences.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark signals the looser definition, effect standing for consequences.
explanation.definitionFit: Impact is the effect or influence something has, which is what its consequences amount to.

clue.text: Shaft George e.g. and have your say clearly

parts.note: St George is England's patron saint, so George is an example of a saint
to air views is to voice them
well can mean clearly or plainly, as in well defined

explanation.surface: Someone called George is told to speak up and be clear.
explanation.walkthrough: George is the saint, abbreviated ST; the surface makes him an ordinary man.
explanation.definitionFit: A stairwell is the vertical shaft in a building around which a staircase runs.

clue.text: Trouble in the underworld? Ruffian mostly rises

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld and a name for the underworld itself

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the letters read from the bottom up
most of the word: its last letter is dropped

parts.note: a brute is a violent thug

explanation.surface: Unrest in the criminal underworld as a hoodlum climbs the ranks.
explanation.walkthrough: The underworld looks like gangland, but it is Dis, Hades in Roman myth.
explanation.definitionFit: To trouble someone is to bother or upset them, a verb synonym.

clue.text: I keep an eye on old boy who's waiting for someone?

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for a former pupil of a school
a server waits on diners, so waits for someone

explanation.surface: A watcher describes themselves as an old boy hanging about for a friend to show up.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue speaks in the first person, so the definition is a description of what the answer does.
explanation.definitionFit: A watcher, monitor or onlooker is one who keeps an eye on things.

clue.text: Born free, baby in turn could be ____?

definitions.text: Born free, baby in turn could be ____?

indicators.note: free means let loose, so these letters are released into a new order

parts.note: taken as written: these letters are the ones rearranged

explanation.surface: A newborn creature, set loose, grows up to become something you fill in.
explanation.walkthrough: The blank is the definition: a newborn baby rabbit, once free, could be this. B is born, as in genealogies.
explanation.definitionFit: A baby or young rabbit, or a child's word for any rabbit, could be described by the whole clue.

clue.text: European male vociferously advocates for issues

indicators.note: loudly spoken, so the word is taken for its sound

parts.note: to urge is to recommend strongly

explanation.surface: A European man noisily campaigns on behalf of causes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issues' looks like a noun, topics; it is the verb, comes out.
explanation.definitionFit: Issues as a verb means comes out or flows forth, the same as appears from somewhere.

clue.text: Record wine borders on likely to be stacked up

parts.note: vin is French for wine

indicators.note: in a down clue, stacked up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards
the borders of the word are its first and last letters

parts.note: its border letters are the first and last ones

explanation.surface: A wine record suggests boxes of bottles likely to be piled high.
explanation.definitionFit: Vinyl is the plastic that gramophone discs are pressed from, so it stands for records.

clue.text: Sideline, for example, filling report

indicators.note: the abbreviation for example sits inside, filling the word for report

parts.note: to relate is to tell or recount

explanation.surface: A player dropped to the sidelines, for instance, takes up a journalist's report.
explanation.definitionFit: To relegate is to demote or push aside to a lesser position, as to sideline someone.

clue.text: Rave over a spire that's been restored

indicators.note: a restored building has been put back together, so the letters of the words are rebuilt in a new order

parts.note: taken as written: the letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone gushes about a church steeple that has been renovated.
explanation.definitionFit: To rave over something is to commend it with enthusiasm, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Gather I dropped catch — outrageous

parts.note: to gather is to deduce or conclude

indicators.note: the letter for I is let fall out of the word for catch

parts.note: to nail someone is to catch them
taken as written, the letter removed

explanation.surface: A cricketer realises they dropped a catch and calls it a scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I dropped catch' reads as a fielder's confession, but 'dropped' tells you to remove I from the word for catch.
explanation.definitionFit: Infernal is used informally for something irritating or shocking, like hellish.

clue.text: Corp truly goes bad like this!

indicators.note: letters that go bad are spoilt and twisted into a different order

parts.note: taken as written: the letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A corporation really does turn rotten, and in this manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corp truly goes bad' both rearranges the letters and describes how a company behaves dishonestly, so the definition 'like this' points back at it.
explanation.definitionFit: An adverb meaning in a dishonest, depraved manner, which is how a company that goes bad behaves.

clue.text: In no time art transformed boundary

indicators.note: something transformed is changed completely, so the letters are remade

parts.note: taken as written: the letters rearranged

explanation.surface: An artwork changed beyond recognition, edge and all, in a flash.
explanation.definitionFit: A termination is an end or limit, which is a sense of boundary, the point where something stops.

clue.text: Perhaps Russian can nearly quaff a gallon

indicators.note: nearly the whole word: its final letter is left off

parts.note: to gulp is to drink down greedily
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Russian can seemingly swallow a whole gallon of drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can' is slang for prison, not a tin; the Gulag was the Soviet labour-camp system.
explanation.definitionFit: Can is slang for jail, and the Gulag was the Soviet system of forced-labour prison camps.

clue.text: Trouble with bread and jam?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: shortage of money, bread being slang for cash
second meaning: an awkward predicament or fix

explanation.walkthrough: Bread and jam suggest a sandwich, but bread is slang for money and jam is a tight spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Financial embarrassment is a lack of funds, and an embarrassment can also be any awkward, difficult situation.

clue.text: Duck below this?

parts.note: the eider is a large sea duck
down means lower or beneath

explanation.surface: An instruction to take cover under something.
explanation.walkthrough: The eider duck's soft breast feathers are its down, used to fill quilts; and you lie below a quilt.
explanation.definitionFit: An eiderdown is a quilt, traditionally stuffed with eider feathers, that you sleep beneath.

clue.text: Summary of Jack's pamphlet

parts.note: a jack or jack tar is a sailor, as is an AB, able seaman
a tract is a short religious or political pamphlet

explanation.surface: A digest of a leaflet written by someone named Jack.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack is a sailor here, a jack tar, giving AB for able seaman.
explanation.definitionFit: An abstract is a brief summary of a paper or report placed at its start.

clue.text: Where to see posts round sort of motor

parts.note: a round is a single bullet of ammunition
an inboard motor is mounted inside a boat's hull

explanation.surface: Sounds like a mechanic's catalogue entry for a type of ammunition and an engine.
explanation.walkthrough: Posts here are messages pinned up or put online, not fence posts or mail.
explanation.definitionFit: Notices and online messages are posted on a noticeboard of this kind, physical or electronic.

clue.text: Scout learning under former leader of patrol

indicators.note: in a down clue, under means placed after the other pieces

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: the leader is the opening letter of patrol

parts.note: the word whose first letter is taken
lore is traditional knowledge and learning

explanation.surface: A boy scout learning under a former patrol leader.
explanation.walkthrough: Scout looks like a noun, a member of a patrol; it is the verb, to reconnoitre.
explanation.definitionFit: To scout an area is to investigate or reconnoitre it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Deliberate promo on Plautus' force that's central to comedies

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above the next piece

parts.note: promo and ad are both short for advertising
vis is Latin for force, and Plautus wrote in Latin

indicators.note: the middle letters of the word are taken

parts.note: an eight-letter word, so its central pair of letters is used

explanation.surface: A deliberate publicity push for Plautus's troupe at the heart of his comedies.
explanation.walkthrough: Plautus was a Roman comic playwright, pointing to the Latin word for force.
explanation.definitionFit: Advised describes an action carefully considered beforehand, as in ill-advised, so intentional.

clue.text: One in America models for Status Quo?

indicators.note: the one goes inside the other pieces

parts.note: artists' models sit for portraits

explanation.surface: An American band member posing for the rock group Status Quo.
explanation.walkthrough: Status Quo is a British rock band, but the definition is the Latin phrase meaning the existing state of things.
explanation.definitionFit: Status quo means things as they currently stand, the unchanged state of affairs.

clue.text: Put your Sunday best on for returning boxer

parts.note: to and for can both mean towards or on behalf of

indicators.note: the word for boxer comes back the other way

parts.note: pug is short for pugilist, a boxer

explanation.surface: A fighter coming back for a bout is told to dress smartly.
explanation.walkthrough: Tog up is British informal for dressing up in smart clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: To tog up is a British colloquial phrasal verb for dressing smartly, as in your finest clothes.

clue.text: Get what literally gives pain from corn?

wordplay.words: what literally gives pain from corn
wordplay.note: corn is grain; putting a P in place of its first two letters gives pain, which is spelt literally as the instruction

explanation.surface: Puzzling over what causes a painful corn on the foot.
explanation.walkthrough: Corn gives GRAIN; written out literally, 'GR as P' turns GRAIN into PAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: To grasp an idea is to understand it, the sense of get as in 'I get it'.

clue.text: It's run via updated software for protection

indicators.note: software that is updated is rewritten, so the letters are rewritten in a new order

parts.note: taken as written: the letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A program running through an update keeps a computer safe.
explanation.definitionFit: An antivirus package is a security program that guards a computer against malicious code.

clue.text: A natural oil being refined near a part of Turkey

indicators.note: next to: the rearranged oil sits beside the final a

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: crude oil being refined is processed and changed, so its letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
taken as written

explanation.surface: Crude oil is processed at a refinery close to a region of Turkey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A natural oil being refined' looks like anagram fodder for the whole answer, but only oil is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Anatolia is the large Asian peninsula forming most of the Turkish land mass.

clue.text: Class fool, otherwise term for clot

parts.note: an ass is a silly person
or introduces an alternative, as otherwise does

indicators.note: a term is an end, so this is the final letter of clot

parts.note: the word whose final letter is taken

explanation.surface: A teacher's insult: the class idiot, or another word for a dimwit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Term for clot' looks like a synonym hunt for clot, but term means the end of clot.
explanation.definitionFit: To assort is to classify or sort items into groups, so a verb sense of class.

clue.text: Settle over bit of change being cheap

indicators.note: turned over, so the word for settle is read backwards

parts.note: to put is to place or lay something down
a penny is a small coin

explanation.surface: Paying a bill with a few coins of change looks like being stingy.
explanation.walkthrough: Tuppenny, from twopenny, is British for worth only two pennies.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tuppenny is worth very little, so it is trivial or inexpensive, like the phrase tuppenny-ha'penny.

clue.text: Pride, perhaps, turning on a complete dandy

indicators.note: placed after, so the reversed sin comes after the other pieces

parts.note: taken as written
to do a job is to complete it

indicators.note: the word for the sin is turned round to read backwards

parts.note: pride is one of the seven deadly sins

explanation.surface: A fop who is wholly vain, his pride turning into a complete show.
explanation.definitionFit: Adonis was the beautiful youth of Greek myth, so the name is used for a handsome, vain young man.
